rv: I was stationed in Japan with the 11th Airborne Division when the airlift started. I remember well how we were wondering if WWIII was about to start. I saw this movie when it came out in 1950. My Division had left Japan and was stationed at Ft. Campbell, Ky. At about that time the Korean War started and I was on my way back to the orient. In February of 1951 I was wounded near the city of Wonju and that ended my military career. This movie brought back so many memories of those days. It is a very good movie and quite true to the times. Definitely worth watching.

rv: 'Born to Gamble' is a pretty good film. Not really a must-see, but still pretty good At the heart of the story, it really shows how most parents truly want the best for their children. I'm not a parent yet, but it wasn't hard for me to imagine the pain and heartache that the parents in this movie must have felt when their children went astray and made bad choices in life, as most kids (and young adults) often do. It's a quite sad at parts, but most good movies are.

Episodic morality tale about the evils of gambling that relies a lot of flashback tales about different tales of gambling and it's consequences in the first half, then dives into a melodramatic tale about a fellow who tries to get revenge on a lout who killed his brother by carrying out a bombastic scheme. rv: As a first time reviewer, I liked this film due to its subject matter, the "Thuds", and its role in the Vietnam War.

High spin factor is in effect for this exploration about what benefits the Air Force is bringing to the Viet Nam war. Of course, this is all Top Gun, making the Air Force look as glamorous as possible. Noone dies, and even if your plane does go down, there will be a Jolly Green Helicopter to come in and scoop you up (complete with gung-ho theme song). Heck, even Mr. Viet-Nam Spin Doctor himself Robert Macnamara makes an appearance.

Although it is a propaganda piece,it has some redeeming qualities. It has some very nice footage of several of the different aircraft that was prevalent in Vietnam. Also,some very nice visuals of a beautiful country torn apart by war. As long as you understand that this is an Air Force propaganda piece,you can enjoy this somewhat entertaining documentary.
